title: Security & Compliance Operational Playbook: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, and Risk Exceptions
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Company-wide operational playbook that consolidates policies and procedures for RBAC and authentication, audit logging and retention, data residency and retention, secure SDLC controls, incident response (security), compliance evidence workflows, and risk & exception handling.
body:
Overview
This playbook defines Redwood Inference’s cross-functional security and compliance controls and operational procedures covering RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure software development lifecycle (SDLC) controls, incident response (security), compliance evidence workflows, and risk & exception handling. The intent is to provide a single reference for engineering, security, product, and compliance teams to ensure consistent controls, measurable evidence collection, and auditable decision trails.

1) Principles and Scope
- Apply least privilege and separation of duties for all production systems.
- Ensure auditability: all privileged actions must be logged and retained according to retention schedules.
- Maintain clear ownership and evidence to support compliance audits (SOC2, ISO27001, contractual obligations).
- Provide documented, time-bound exceptions where full controls cannot be met, with compensating controls.
- Scope: this document applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and to all Redwood-managed control planes and customer-facing administrative tooling.

2) RBAC and Authentication
Purpose: Define role definitions, authorization model, onboarding/offboarding, review cadence, emergency access, and MFA requirements.

Roles and Permission Model- Roles (examples):
  - platform-admin: full control over infra and deployment orchestration (limited to SRE/platform team members).
  - security-admin: manage security tooling, audit logs, alerts, and incident response.
  - svc-account: machine/service identities used by pipelines and runtime components.
  - dev: developer-level access to non-prod namespaces and CI logs.
  - customer-admin: customer-scoped admin for Dedicated/Private deployments with appropriate tenancy boundaries.

- Permissions use a resource-action model (resource:project,cluster,model; action:read,write,deploy,admin).
- No role should grant both deploy and billing/admin rights by default.
- Service accounts must be scoped to the minimal set of resources and use short-lived credentials where supported.

Onboarding / Offboarding Processes- New human accounts require SSO + enforced MFA (FIDO2 or TOTP).
- Access requests follow the access-requests workflow: request -> manager approval -> role owner approval -> access provisioned by IAM service.
- Offboarding: HR/security trigger automated deprovisioning for terminated accounts; cloud keys rotated within 4 hours of offboarding.

Periodic Reviews and Certifications- Quarterly role membership review with owners.
- Automated alerts for stale privileges (90-day inactivity flagged).
- Annual certification for all users with access to production environments.

Emergency/Elevated Access (Break glass)- Break-glass requests must be submitted in the emergency access system, require justification, must be time-limited, and are recorded in audit logs.
- Post-use review required within 72 hours by security and the affected team.

Authentication Standards- Single Sign-On (SSO) via corporate IdP (SAML 2.0 / OIDC).
- MFA required for all interactive users.
- Passwords not permitted for privileged accounts.

3) Audit Logging and Log Management
Scope: All privileged actions, administrative API calls, configuration changes, data exports, and scheduler/job executions affecting production must be logged.

Log Types and Events to Capture- Authentication events: login, logout, MFA failures, token issuance.
- Authorization events: role changes, policy updates, permission grants and revocations.
- Administrative actions: deployment rollouts, config changes, secrets rotation, user provisioning.
- Data access events: exports, queries that access protected datasets, backup restores.
- System-level events: service crashes, autoscaler actions, capacity scaling.

Log Format and Integrity- Logs must be structured JSON with consistent schema (timestamp, actor, actor_id, actor_role, action, resource, resource_id, outcome, trace_id).
- All logs forwarded to centralized log store / SIEM (configured for immutable append-only retention where possible).
- Log integrity: write-once storage (WORM) for audit-critical logs; periodic cryptographic hashing of log buckets.

Retention and Access Controls- Retention table:
| Event type                 | Primary retention | Archive retention | Notes |
|---------------------------|-------------------:|------------------:|-------|
| Authentication events     | 1 year             | 7 years           | Auth logs required for incident forensics and audits |
| Authorization changes     | 3 years            | 7 years           | Includes RBAC changes and approvals |
| Administrative actions    | 3 years            | 7 years           | Deployment and configuration changes |
| Data access / exports     | 7 years            | 10 years          | For compliance with contractual obligations |

- Access to logs is role-restricted; only security and designated SREs have read access to unredacted audit logs.
- Sensitive logs that contain PII or secrets must be redacted before wide access.

Alerting and Monitoring- Define log-based alerts for: unusual privilege escalations, large data exports, repeated failed authentications, and cross-region configuration changes.
- All alerts feed into the security incident queue with defined SLA for triage (15 minutes for high-severity).

4) Data Residency and Retention
Residency Controls- Data classification drives residency decisions: customer_data (subject to customer-region constraints), telemetry/metrics (aggregated, stored regionally), backups (copied per region policy).
- For customers with residency requirements, deploy control plane and storage resources in required cloud regions and enforce egress restrictions.

Data Retention & Deletion- Default retention policy: customer metadata and logs follow retention table above; customer-submitted data retention defaults to 365 days unless contractually specified.
- Data deletion workflow: deletion request -> validation -> removal from primary store -> purge from backups according to backup retention policy -> update evidence logs.
- Legal hold: legal or compliance can place data on hold which overrides deletion schedules; holds documented with owner and expiry.

Backups and Replica Management- Backups are encrypted at rest with KMS-managed keys and stored within the customer-designated region where required.
- Backup retention and replication follows the backup policy matrix with owner approval for cross-region replication.

5) Secure SDLC Controls
Goals: Shift left security, ensure reproducible builds, and maintain an auditable pipeline from code commit to production.

Gates and Requirements- Pre-merge checks: static analysis (SAST), dependency scanning, linting, and unit test coverage thresholds.
- CI pipeline: reproducible builds, artifact signing, container image scanning for CVEs, and SBOM generation.
- Staging/Canary: DAST and integration tests against representative data; canary rollouts with metrics/health checks before full production deployment.
- Release approval: release owner, security sign-off (if high-risk changes), and documented rollback plan.

Tooling and Evidence- Mandatory tools: SAST (code scanner), dependency scanner (software composition analysis), container scanner, IaC scanner, secrets detection.
- CI artifacts (build IDs, SBOMs, scan reports) are archived for compliance evidence with links recorded in release records.

Developer Security Checklist (pre-release)
1. All new dependencies scanned and approved.
2. No high/critical CVEs in production artifacts unless an approved exception exists.
3. Secrets removed from code and validated by secret scanner.
4. DB migrations reviewed and staged in canary.
5. Rollback plan validated and smoke tests defined.

6) Incident Response (Security) Procedures
Objective: Provide repeatable, auditable steps for detecting, triaging, containing, eradicating, recovering from, and reporting security incidents.

Incident lifecycle- Detection & Alerting: security tooling, SIEM, alerts from monitoring teams, user reports.
- Triage: assign severity (P0,P1,P2), determine affected systems and data, assemble incident response (IR) team.
- Containment: temporary network segmentation, credential rotation, revoke tokens, disable compromised service accounts.
- Eradication & Recovery: apply fixes, rotate keys, validate fixes in staging, restore services, and monitor for recurrence.
- Post-incident: formal postmortem within 7 business days, RCA, timeline, corrective actions, and closure.

Communication- Internal comms: page appropriate stakeholders via incident channels and maintain an incident status page.
- External comms: follow legal and compliance guidance for notification to affected customers and regulators. Public statements require approval from Legal + Head of Security + Communications.

Forensic Evidence Handling- Preserve forensic images and logs in WORM storage; document chain of custody for collected artifacts.
- Any PII or customer data accessed during investigation must be recorded and minimized.

Incident Playbook (high-level steps)
1. Detect and validate alert.
2. Triage severity and scope.
3. Engage IR team and assign roles (Incident Commander, Communications, Engineering Lead, Forensics).
4. Contain: isolate impacted infrastructure and rotate credentials.
5. Eradicate root cause and implement fixes.
6. Recover and validate system integrity.
7. Conduct postmortem and file evidence artifacts to the compliance evidence repository.

7) Compliance Evidence Workflows
Objective: Ensure evidence for controls is collected, stored, and accessible for audits (SOC2, ISO/PCI where applicable).

Evidence Catalog and Owners- Every control in the control matrix has a named evidence owner responsible for producing and refreshing evidence.
- Example evidence types: access review logs, RBAC change tickets, CI pipeline SBOMs, vulnerability scan results, incident postmortems, customer contract residency clauses.

Collection & Storage Process
- Evidence captured must be immutable (timestamped), contain a link to the source artifact, and include owner and retention metadata.
- Primary storage: compliance evidence repo (encrypted, access-restricted).
- Evidence refresh cadence: quarterly for operational controls; immediate capture for incident-related evidence.

Audit Support and Request Handling
- For audit requests, compliance will surface a collection bundle that includes required artifacts and owner attestations.
- SLAs: operational controls evidence delivered within 5 business days; deeper technical artifacts within 15 business days unless exceptions are granted.

8) Risk & Exceptions Process
Purpose: Allow controlled and documented deviations from standard controls when necessary.

Requesting an Exception
- Submit an exception request via the risk register portal with: description, affected controls, justification, compensating controls, risk owner, proposed expiry, and rollback plan.
- Template fields: request_id, owner, justification, compensating_controls, expiration_date, approved_by, approval_date, residual_risk_rating.

Approval & Review
- Risk committee reviews requests weekly; high-risk or long-duration exceptions require executive approval (CISO + Head of Product).
- All exceptions receive a residual risk rating and mandatory compensating controls.

Expiration and Renewal
- Exceptions automatically expire on the agreed date and must be renewed with evidence of mitigation progress.
- Quarterly monitoring reports for active exceptions and a mandatory remediation plan tracked in the risk register.

9) Roles and Ownership Summary
- Security: policy owner, incident commander escalation, evidence owner for security controls.
- Eng SRE/Platform: implement and operate RBAC, log collection, and backups.
- Product: approve customer residency and data retention terms.
- Legal/Compliance: manage audit requests, legal holds, and regulatory notifications.
- Team Owners: maintain evidence and run quarterly control reviews.

Appendix A: Sample Exception Request (text form)
- request_id: EXC-2025-0042
- owner: team-name@redwood.com
- justification: Temporary need to allow legacy service account to access cross-project artifacts to complete migration.
- compensating_controls: limited network egress, time-limited token, daily alerting on activity, code access review.
- expiration_date: 2025-03-01

Appendix B: Evidence Checklist for Annual Audit
- Current RBAC membership export (CSV) with owner attestations.
- Last 12 months of admin action logs.
- Two most recent vulnerability scan reports and remediation tickets.
- Sample signed release artifact and SBOM.
- Incident postmortems for P1/P0 incidents in the period.
